recipes.title: Spaghetti bolognese, light
recipes.summary: A slow-simmered beef and tomato ragu bulked out with mushrooms and courgette, over a modest tangle of spaghetti.

steps.instruction: Finely dice the onion, carrot and celery, chop the mushrooms small, and dice the courgette. Keeping the mushrooms fine matters here — they should melt into the sauce and read as meat rather than as vegetables.

Warm the olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat and cook the onion, carrot and celery until soft and translucent but not coloured, about 8 minutes. Stir in the garlic for the last minute, until it smells sweet rather than raw.

Turn the heat up, add the beef and break it apart with a wooden spoon. Cook until no pink remains and the base of the pan is browning, about 6 minutes. Add the mushrooms and courgette and cook until they release their liquid.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for a minute so it darkens, then add the tinned tomatoes and beef stock. Season well and bring to a bare simmer.
Leave to simmer uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the sauce is thick and glossy and no longer watery at the edges. This is where the flavour comes from — do not rush it.
Cook the spaghetti in well-salted boiling water until al dente, then drain, saving a cupful of the water.
Toss the drained pasta through the sauce, loosening with a splash of the reserved water until it coats every strand. Serve with the parmesan grated over.

recipes.storageNotes: Keeps well and improves overnight. Cool quickly, refrigerate, and reheat gently with a splash of water. Freeze the sauce alone, not the pasta.

recipes.title: Spaghetti bolognese
recipes.summary: The proper thing: beef softened in milk, a long simmer with tomatoes and soffritto, and enough spaghetti to make it a real dinner.

steps.instruction: Finely dice the onion, carrot and celery. Keep the dice small and even — this is the base of the sauce and large pieces stay noticeable to the end.
Warm the olive oil in a heavy pan over medium heat and cook the onion, carrot and celery gently until soft, sweet and translucent, about 10 minutes. Add the garlic for the final minute.
Raise the heat, add the beef, and break it up as it cooks. Let it brown properly rather than steam — you want colour on the base of the pan, about 7 minutes.
Pour in the milk and simmer until it has almost entirely disappeared. This is the step people skip; it is what makes the meat tender rather than grainy.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for a minute, then add the tinned tomatoes and beef stock. Season generously and bring to a bare simmer.
Simmer uncovered, stirring now and then, until thick, glossy and darkened, with oil beginning to separate at the edges.
Cook the spaghetti in well-salted boiling water until al dente. Drain, keeping a cupful of the cooking water.
Toss the pasta through the sauce over low heat, loosening with the reserved water until it clings. Finish with the grated parmesan.

recipes.storageNotes: Better the next day. Cool quickly and refrigerate. The sauce freezes well on its own; cook fresh pasta to serve with it.

recipes.title: Spaghetti bolognese, hearty
recipes.summary: The same ragu built bigger, with pancetta for depth and a generous plate of spaghetti underneath.

steps.instruction: Finely dice the onion, carrot and celery, and dice the cured pork small.
Render the cured pork in the olive oil over medium heat until the fat runs and the edges crisp, about 5 minutes.
Add the onion, carrot and celery and cook until soft and translucent, about 10 minutes, stirring in the garlic for the last minute.
Raise the heat, add the beef, and break it up. Brown it properly — you want real colour, about 8 minutes.
Pour in the milk and simmer until almost fully absorbed.
Stir in the tomato paste, cook for a minute, then add the tinned tomatoes and beef stock. Season and bring to a bare simmer.
Simmer uncovered until thick, dark and glossy, with the fat starting to separate.
Cook the spaghetti in well-salted boiling water until al dente. Drain, reserving a cupful of the water.
Toss the pasta through the sauce, loosening with the reserved water, and finish with the parmesan.

recipes.storageNotes: Keeps three days refrigerated and reheats well with a splash of water. Freeze the sauce alone for up to three months.

recipes.title: Thai green chicken curry, light
recipes.summary: Fragrant green curry loosened with broth instead of extra coconut milk, packed with greens and served over a modest scoop of rice.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice until the water runs clear, then set it to cook by your usual method.

Heat the vegetable oil in a wide pan and fry the green curry paste over medium heat until it darkens and smells strongly aromatic, about 2 minutes. This step is what separates a good curry from a flat one.
Add the sliced chicken and turn it through the paste until the outsides are opaque, about 5 minutes.
Pour in the coconut milk and chicken broth, bring to a gentle simmer, and cook until the chicken is cooked through, about 8 minutes.
Add the green beans and courgette and simmer until just tender but still with bite, about 6 minutes.
Stir through the spinach until it wilts, then season with the fish sauce, brown sugar and lime juice. Taste and adjust — it should be salty, sour and faintly sweet all at once.
Let the rice steam undisturbed while the curry settles off the heat.
Tear the basil over the curry and serve with the rice.

recipes.storageNotes: Best eaten fresh, as the vegetables soften on reheating. Keeps two days refrigerated. Do not freeze — the coconut milk splits.

recipes.title: Thai green chicken curry
recipes.summary: Chicken simmered in coconut milk with green curry paste, green beans and bamboo, finished with lime and basil over jasmine rice.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice until the water runs clear and set it to cook.

Spoon the thick cream from the top of the coconut milk tin into a wide pan with the vegetable oil. Fry the green curry paste in it over medium heat until it darkens and the oil separates, about 3 minutes.
Add the sliced chicken and turn it through the paste until the surfaces turn opaque, about 5 minutes.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk, bring to a gentle simmer and cook until the chicken is cooked through, about 8 minutes. Keep it below a rolling boil or the sauce will split.
Add the green beans and bamboo shoots and simmer until the beans are tender with a little bite left, about 6 minutes.
Season with the fish sauce, brown sugar and lime juice, then taste. It should land salty, sour and faintly sweet together.
Let the rice steam undisturbed while the curry rests off the heat.
Tear the basil over the top and serve with the rice.

recipes.storageNotes: Keeps two days refrigerated and reheats gently over low heat. Not suitable for freezing — coconut milk separates when thawed.

recipes.title: Thai green chicken curry, hearty
recipes.summary: A bigger bowl of green curry with more chicken, cashews for richness and a full plate of jasmine rice.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice until the water runs clear and set it to cook.
Toast the cashews in a dry pan over medium heat until golden and fragrant, then tip them out and set aside.
Spoon the thick coconut cream into the pan with the vegetable oil and fry the green curry paste until it darkens and the oil separates, about 3 minutes.
Add the chicken thigh and turn it through the paste until the surfaces are opaque, about 6 minutes.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk and simmer gently until the chicken is cooked through and tender, about 10 minutes.
Add the green beans and bamboo shoots and simmer until the beans are just tender, about 6 minutes.
Season with the fish sauce, brown sugar and lime juice and taste to balance.
Let the rice steam undisturbed while the curry rests.
Scatter over the toasted cashews, tear the basil on top, and serve with the rice.

recipes.storageNotes: Keeps two days refrigerated. Add the cashews fresh on reheating so they stay crisp. Not suitable for freezing.

recipes.title: Teriyaki salmon rice bowl, light
recipes.summary: Glazed salmon over rice with a generous pile of steamed broccoli and cucumber, using just enough glaze to lacquer the fish.

steps.instruction: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and set it to cook.
Stir together the soy sauce, rice wine, brown sugar, grated ginger and minced garlic to make the glaze.
Steam the broccoli florets until bright green and just tender to the point of a knife, about 5 minutes. Slice the cucumber while it steams.
Heat the sesame oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat and cook the salmon skin-side down until the skin is crisp, about 4 minutes, then turn.
Pour the glaze into the pan and spoon it over the fish as it bubbles and thickens, about 3 minutes, until the salmon is just opaque at the centre and lacquered.
Let the rice steam undisturbed off the heat.
Fluff the rice into bowls, top with the salmon, broccoli and cucumber, spoon over the pan glaze and scatter with sesame seeds and spring onions.

recipes.storageNotes: Best eaten fresh. Keeps one day refrigerated and is good cold the next day. Do not freeze.

recipes.title: Teriyaki salmon rice bowl
recipes.summary: Salmon glazed in soy, mirin and ginger until lacquered, served over rice with steamed broccoli and sesame.

steps.instruction: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and set it to cook.
Stir together the soy sauce, rice wine, brown sugar, grated ginger and minced garlic to make the glaze.
Steam the broccoli florets until bright green and just tender, about 5 minutes.
Heat the sesame oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat and cook the salmon skin-side down until the skin crisps and releases from the pan, about 4 minutes, then turn it over.

Pour in the glaze and spoon it over the salmon as it bubbles and thickens to a syrup, about 3 minutes. The fish is ready when it flakes at the thickest point but is still faintly translucent at the very centre.
Let the rice steam undisturbed off the heat.
Fluff the rice into bowls, top with salmon and broccoli, pour over the remaining pan glaze, and finish with sesame seeds and spring onions.

recipes.storageNotes: Best eaten fresh while the skin is crisp. Keeps one day refrigerated and eats well cold. Do not freeze.

recipes.title: Teriyaki salmon rice bowl, hearty
recipes.summary: A larger fillet, a fuller bowl of rice and a soft-boiled egg alongside — the same glazed salmon, built for a bigger appetite.

steps.instruction: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and set it to cook.
Lower the eggs into boiling water and cook for 7 minutes for a just-set jammy yolk, then cool them under cold running water and peel.
Stir together the soy sauce, rice wine, brown sugar, grated ginger and minced garlic to make the glaze.
Steam the broccoli florets until bright green and just tender, about 5 minutes.
Heat the sesame oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat and cook the salmon skin-side down until crisp, about 5 minutes, then turn.
Add the glaze and spoon it over the fish as it thickens, about 3 minutes, until the salmon is lacquered and just cooked through.
Let the rice steam undisturbed off the heat.
Fluff the rice into bowls, add the salmon, broccoli and halved eggs, spoon over the pan glaze and finish with sesame seeds and spring onions.

recipes.storageNotes: Best eaten fresh. Keeps one day refrigerated; store the egg separately. Do not freeze.

recipes.title: Hummus and vegetable plate, light
recipes.summary: Smooth lemony hummus with a pile of raw vegetables for scooping and a small wedge of warm pita.

steps.instruction: Drain and rinse the chickpeas well. Rinsing matters — the starchy tinning liquid makes hummus taste dull.

Blend the chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, olive oil and cumin in a food processor with a good pinch of salt, adding cold water a tablespoon at a time until it turns pale and smooth. It should be looser than you think — it firms up as it sits.
Cut the carrot and cucumber into sticks and slice the pepper.
Warm the pita briefly and cut into wedges. Spread the hummus into a shallow bowl and serve with the vegetables and pita alongside.

recipes.storageNotes: The hummus keeps four days refrigerated under a film of olive oil. Cut the vegetables fresh. Hummus freezes well for a month.

recipes.title: Hummus and vegetable plate
recipes.summary: Properly smooth hummus, rich with tahini and olive oil, served with crunchy raw vegetables and warm pita.

steps.instruction: Drain and rinse the chickpeas thoroughly, discarding the tinning liquid.

Blend the chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, half the olive oil and the cumin with a good pinch of salt. Trickle in cold water a spoonful at a time and keep the machine running until the hummus turns visibly paler and completely smooth, about 3 minutes.
Cut the carrot and cucumber into sticks and slice the pepper.

Warm the pitas and cut into wedges. Spread the hummus in a shallow bowl, make a hollow in the middle with the back of a spoon, pour the remaining olive oil into it and serve with the vegetables and pita.

recipes.storageNotes: Keeps four days refrigerated under a film of olive oil, which stops the surface drying out. Freezes for a month; loosen with water after thawing.

recipes.title: Hummus and vegetable plate, hearty
recipes.summary: A full mezze plate: rich hummus topped with warm spiced chickpeas and toasted pine nuts, with plenty of pita and vegetables.

steps.instruction: Drain and rinse all the chickpeas, setting aside a third of them for the topping.

Blend the larger portion of chickpeas with the tahini, lemon juice, garlic, two thirds of the olive oil and the cumin, plus a good pinch of salt. Add cold water a spoonful at a time until pale and completely smooth.
Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan over medium heat until golden, watching closely as they catch quickly. Tip them out.
In the same pan, warm the reserved chickpeas in the remaining olive oil with the paprika until hot and slightly blistered, about 4 minutes.
Cut the carrot and cucumber into sticks and slice the pepper.
Warm the pitas and cut into wedges. Spread the hummus in a shallow bowl, pile the warm spiced chickpeas into the centre, scatter over the pine nuts, and serve with the vegetables and pita.

recipes.storageNotes: The hummus base keeps four days refrigerated under olive oil. Warm the chickpea topping and toast the nuts fresh each time.
